label: prf:sw-classical-jet-exactness
title: Proof that the classical-jet prolongation is exact and period-free
html:
The fibre coordinate X is a meromorphic function on \Sigma, and the total derivative along the curve of a meromorphic function is meromorphic (at a ramification point with local coordinate t, where z = z_c + t^2, the first jet acquires a pole: X^{(1)} = \frac{dX/dt}{dz/dt}; higher jets acquire poles of higher order). Hence each X^{(n-1)}, n \ge 1, is a meromorphic function on \Sigma, and

\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} \;=\; X^{(n)}\,dz \;=\; \frac{d}{dz}\bigl(X^{(n-1)}\bigr)\,dz \;=\; d\bigl(X^{(n-1)}\bigr)

is exact.

Exactness kills residues: in a local coordinate t at any p \in \Sigma, write X^{(n-1)} = \sum_k c_k t^k with finite principal part; then d(X^{(n-1)}) = \sum_k k\,c_k\,t^{k-1}\,dt contains no t^{-1}\,dt term (the k = 0 term differentiates to zero and every other term lands away from t^{-1}), so \mathrm{Res}_p\,\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} = 0. Exactness kills periods: \oint_\gamma d(X^{(n-1)}) = 0 for every closed cycle \gamma avoiding the poles of X^{(n-1)}, by Stokes' theorem on the curve. The residue-sum period of prop:sw-period-residue-sum is 2\pi i times a sum of these vanishing residues, hence zero at every vertical degree n \ge 1.

The final claim follows because the classical binding period is nonzero: at q = 1, a_D^{(m)} = \mathrm{lw}(m-1) = I(m)/m > 0 with I(m) the involution numbers (Lean involutionNumber_pos), and a vanishing period cannot equal a nonzero number. The Lean witness QOU.Brings.classical_jet_period_zero proves the coefficient-level core (fresidue_fderiv: the t^{-1} coefficient of a termwise derivative vanishes, over a generic commutative ring) and composes it with the residue-sum hypothesis; classical_jet_period_ne_lw concludes the non-realisability. \qquad\blacksquare
